name: Tertiary Button
propertyCopy: Set the button’s size, content, corners and label.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Tertiary Button is the lowest-emphasis boxed action in the system - text-only styling with no fill and no border at rest, used for actions that should be available but never compete visually with Primary or Secondary. When to Use Low-priority actions alongside higher-emphasis buttons - Learn More, Skip, View More. Secondary navigation inside a flow - Advanced Settings, a link to an optional step. Repeated actions in a dense layout - where even Secondary's border would add too much visual noise. When Not to Use The main or supporting action of a screen - use Primary or Secondary so the hierarchy stays legible. Irreversible actions - always use Destructive, regardless of how minor the action seems. Anywhere the action needs strong discoverability - a Tertiary button can be easy to miss; use Secondary if visibility matters. Best Practices Reserve it for genuinely optional or low-stakes actions, not as a default fallback for anything without a clear priority. Still give it a real hit target and visible focus ring even though it has no border at rest. Avoid using more than one or two Tertiary buttons in the same row - it starts to read as a wall of plain text otherwise. Do and Don't Do EditView history The lowest-emphasis option in a row that already has a stronger action above it, so the hierarchy reads top to bottom. Don't Confirm purchase A Tertiary standing alone as the only way to complete a purchase is nearly invisible. The most important action on the screen needs more than a Tertiary's weight. Accessibility Still a native <button> element with the same keyboard behavior as every other button type. Focus and hover states add a visible background or underline change, since the rest state alone has very little contrast to lean on. Label text still meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast against the surrounding panel.
